title: Fairly heavy rainfall expected in several provinces
byline: The Department of meteorology says that atmospheric conditions will be favorable for afternoon thundershowers in most parts of the island.

title: Trump fires Pam Bondi as US Attorney General
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump ousted Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday after mounting frustration with her performance, especially over the release of files on late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

title: Trump: ‘Bridges next, then Electric Power Plants!’
byline: Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social, saying the army “hasn’t even started destroying what’s left in Iran”.

title: Artemis capsule boost puts astronauts moon-bound for record-breaking journey
byline: The Orion capsule carrying four astronauts in NASA’s Artemis II mission executed a key thruster firing on Thursday that will kick the crew out of Earth’s orbit and on a path toward the moon, committing them to reaching the farthest distance humans have ever traveled in space.

title: US Army chief of staff fired by Hegseth, sources say
byline: U.S. Army Chief of Staff Randy George was fired on Thursday by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, two U.S. ‌defense officials and a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, in the latest purge among the Pentagon’s most senior ranks.

title: Details of scheduled water cuts in Colombo District today
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced that water supply interruptions will continue in several areas within the Colombo District today (April 3) due to the prevailing dry weather conditions affecting the island.

title: ‘Be serious... don’t speak every day’: Macron criticises Trump approach to Iran war
byline: The Iran war requires a “serious” approach that does not change every day, Emmanuel Macron has said, in an apparent reference to US President Donald Trump’s seemingly contradictory remarks about the conflict.

title: Dinosaur collagen used to create one-of-a-kind handbag
byline: Scientists and designers unveiled on Thursday a handbag made with collagen derived from Tyrannosaurus rex fossils from the U.S. in a unique creation intended to demonstrate the value of laboratory-grown leather.

title: TPA MPs meet President to discuss Malayagam community issues
byline: A group of Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA) members, including its leader MP Mano Ganesan, met President Anura Kumara Dissanayake this morning (02) at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Final rites of late Mahinda Wijesekera to be held on Saturday
byline: The final rites of former Minister Mahinda Wijesekera will be performed on Saturday (04).

title: SpaceX reportedly files plans for massive IPO
byline: SpaceX, the Elon Musk-owned rocket company that merged earlier this year with his artificial intelligence company xAI, confidentially filed plans for an initial public offering Wednesday in what might be the largest of all time, according to multiple reports.

title: US Embassy warns Iran-aligned militias could attack Baghdad
byline: The US embassy in Iraq has warned that Iran-aligned militant groups may conduct attacks in central Baghdad in the next 24-48 hours, again urging Americans to leave the country.

title: Three arrested over illegal vehicle possession and forged documents racket
byline: Three individuals have been arrested by the Western Province North Crimes Division for possessing vehicles without valid registration licenses, police stated.

title: Guidelines to be introduced for public officials carrying out duties online
byline: The third meeting of the Cabinet-appointed committee tasked with ensuring the continuous functioning of the public service was held under the patronage of Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya, via virtual platform.

title: Former SriLankan CEO Kapila Chandrasena further remanded
byline: The Colombo Magistrate’s Court has rejected the bail application of former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena, who is in remand in custody over allegations of accepting bribes in connection with the purchase of Airbus aircraft.

title: Iran war economic shocks will last ‘months’, says Australia’s PM
byline: Australia’s Prime Minister has warned the economic shock from the war involving Iran will “be with us for months”, as he delivered a rare televised address to the nation.

title: Detention orders on 6 fishermen arrested over Rs. 6 billion drug haul
byline: A court has granted approval to detain and question the six fishermen who were arrested with over 300 kilograms of heroin during a Sri Lanka Navy surveillance operation in the deep seas off Beruwala.

title: Four sentenced to death over three long-running murder cases
byline: The Nuwara Eliya High Court has sentenced four suspects to death in connection with three separate protracted murder cases.

title: IMF delegation meets Speaker and party leaders in Parliament, discuss key issues
byline: A delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) met with the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and Party Leaders of Parliament in preparation for the upcoming IMF Fifth and Sixth Review Mission scheduled from March 26 to April 8, 2026.

title: Schoolboy killed, another critically injured en route to big match in Kandy
byline: A Grade 12 schoolboy has been killed while another student sustained injuries in a tragic accident early this morning (02) when their motorbike collided with a bus on the Kandy–Digana road near the Pallakele Army Camp, police stated.

title: Five injured after van plunges into precipice near Gerandi Ella
byline: Five individuals have sustained serious injuries after a van carrying members of the same family veered off the road and plunged nearly 70 feet down a precipice near the Gerandi Ella area in Kotmale in the early hours of today (02), police stated.

title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calls for national drive to restore infrastructure
byline: Iran’s Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, has called for a comprehensive nationwide drive to restore infrastructure and address the destruction caused by ‘‘unprovoked American-Zionist aggression,’’ state broadcaster Press TV reported.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Northwestern, and Uva provinces, and in Galle, Matara, and Anuradhapura districts.

title: Global oil prices rise after Trump address
byline: Trump’s address appears to have done nothing to reassure global oil markets that disruption to the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route will ease anytime soon.

title: Special committee appointed to monitor and manage drinking water shortage
byline: A special operations committee has been appointed to monitor and manage the ongoing drinking water shortage by the Chairman and General Manager of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board.

title: Gold prices fall as Trump gives no clarity on ending Iran war
byline: Gold prices reversed course to slip more than 1% on Thursday, snapping a four-day winning streak, after U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States would continue the war in Iran over the coming weeks.

title: Sri Lanka appoints new national bowling coach and fielding, spin bowling coach
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has appointed former Netherlands coach Ryan van Niekerk as the National Bowling Coach and Jordan Gregory as the National Fielding and Spin Bowling Coach at the SLC’s National High Performance Centre.

title: Former Minister Mahinda Wijesekara passes away aged 83
byline: Former Cabinet Minister and prominent Southern politician Mahinda Wijesekara has passed away this morning (02) at the age of 83.

title: President-IMF delegation discuss fifth and sixth review under EFF programme
byline: The visiting delegation of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) met with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat today (02) to discuss Sri Lanka’s ongoing economic reform programme and progress under the IMF-supported Extended Fund Facility.

title: New Chief of Staff of Sri Lanka Army appointed
byline: Major General Manada Yahampath of the Sri Lanka Light Infantry has been appointed as the 68th Chief of Staff of the Sri Lanka Army, with effect from today (02), according to Sri Lanka Army.

title: NATO chief to visit Washington next week as Trump threatens exit from alliance
byline: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte will visit Washington next week for what a spokesperson for the military alliance called a ‘‘long-planned visit’’ that comes after President Donald Trump blasted European allies over differences on the Iran war.

title: 14 arrested in four-hour anti-drug operation in Mount Lavinia
byline: At least 14 individuals have been arrested during a special operation conducted in the Badowita areas 1, 2, and 3 within the Mount Lavinia Police Division.

title: UK to host multi-nation meeting on Hormuz shipping
byline: Britain will on Thursday (Apr 2) hold a virtual meeting of about 35 countries to discuss how to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz which has been crippled by the Middle East war.

title: Open warrants issued for Shamindra Rajapaksa, Kapila Chandrasena’s wife over Airbus bribery case
byline: The Colombo Magistrate’s Court today (02) has ordered the issuance of open warrants for the arrest of Shamindra Rajapaksa, a former board member of SriLankan Airlines and son of former Minister Chamal Rajapaksa, and Priyanka Niyomali Wijenayake...

title: Sri Lanka, Russia discuss enhancing multifaceted cooperation at 11th Bilateral Consultations
byline: Sri Lanka and Russia has convened the 11th Round of Bilateral Political Consultations today (2) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment & Tourism of Sri Lanka in Colombo.

title: Nuwan Thushara files case seeking NOC to play in 2026 IPL and other leagues
byline: Fast bowler Nuwan Thushara has filed a petition before the Colombo District Court seeking an order directing Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) to issue a “no objection certificate”, enabling him to participate in international league tournaments, including the 2026 Indian Premier League.

title: Sri Lanka and World Bank launch new partnership to create jobs, attract private investment
byline: The World Bank Group and the Government of Sri Lanka today (03) launched a new five-year Country Partnership Framework (CPF) to support Sri Lanka’s continued recovery, help achieve its 7% medium-term economic growth target, and support job creation.

title: Priceless ancient golden helmet stolen from a Dutch museum is recovered
byline: A priceless ancient golden helmet from Romania stolen last year from a museum in the Netherlands has been recovered, Dutch authorities said Thursday.

title: 3-hour water cuts every other day in Battaramulla, Pamankada, Wellawatte and Nawala
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) says that three-hour water cuts will be imposed in Battaramulla, Pamankada, Wellawatte, Nawala and surrounding areas on every other day from today (April 2) until April 10 from 10.00 p.m. to 1.00 a.m.

title: Indian Govt. waives customs duty on petrochemicals till June 30
byline: The central government on Thursday exempted a wide range of critical petrochemical products till June 30th, in light of the ongoing war in the Middle East and the consequent disruptions in global supply chains.

title: Authorities warn of possible water cuts as Kalatuwawa and Labugama supplies decline
byline: The Kalatuwawa Water Treatment Plant, which is one of the main facilities supplying clean drinking water to the Colombo city and its surrounding areas, has only about 20 days’ worth of water remaining, the Chairman of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board, Engineer Chandana Bandara stated today (02).

title: New guidelines issued to safeguard student welfare and discipline in schools
byline: The Ministry of Education has issued a new circular outlining measures to ensure discipline within schools.

title: 24-hour water cut to several areas in Colombo from tonight
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced a series of 24-hour water cuts affecting several areas due to ongoing water shortages.

title: UK-led 40-nation coalition demands end to Hormuz blockade
byline: The United Kingdom has convened foreign ministers from 40 nations to deliberate on strategies for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial maritime artery currently obstructed by the ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.

title: Agrarian Insurance Board introduces dedicated insurance scheme for divers
byline: The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board, operating under the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land, and Irrigation, has introduced a dedicated insurance scheme for divers.

title: Sri Lanka reports significant drop in tourist arrivals for March 2026
byline: The Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) reports a significant decline in the number of foreign tourists who visited Sri Lanka in March 2026.

title: Canadian national arrested at BIA with over 21kg of Kush cannabis
byline: A foreign passenger attempting to smuggle a consignment of ‘Kush’ cannabis, estimated to be valued at Rs. 217.79 million, into Sri Lanka was arrested by officers of the Police Narcotics Bureau (PNB) at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in the early hours today (April 3).

title: Nine suspects arrested over homicide in Mattakkuliya
byline: A total of nine suspects were arrested yesterday (April 2) by the Sri Lanka Police in connection with the fatal stabbing of an individual in the Mattakkuliya area.

title: Agrarian Service Centers to operate on holidays for Yala season fertilizer distribution
byline: The Department of Agrarian Development has announced that Agrarian Service Centers will remain operational on public holidays to facilitate the distribution of fertilizer to farmers in areas where Yala season paddy cultivation has commenced.

title: Gazette issued on emergency importation of GR 11 rice varieties
byline: The Government of Sri Lanka has issued a Gazette notification to address the looming shortage of Samba and Keeri Samba rice by authorizing the immediate importation of specific substitute varieties.

title: Iconic 19th Century painting sets Indian art record with $17.9m sale
byline: A 19th Century painting by iconic artist Raja Ravi Varma has become the most expensive Indian artwork ever sold, setting a new auction record.

title: Govt halts divestment of eight major SOEs, SC informed
byline: The Attorney General’s Department has informed the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka that the incumbent government will not proceed with the previous government’s decision to divest eight major State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), including Sri Lanka Telecom, SriLankan Airlines, Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation, and Lanka Hospitals.

title: 147 foreign nationals arrested over operating online financial scams
byline: Sri Lanka Police have arrested a total of 147 foreign nationals in connection with an organized online financial scam operation.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Northwestern, Northcentral and Uva provinces, and in Trincomalee, Mannar, Vavuniya and Mullaittivu districts.

title: Chinese national arrested at BIA for attempting to smuggle ‘Kothala Himbutu’
byline: A Chinese national who attempted to smuggle a consignment of Salacia reticulata (Kothala Himbutu), an indigenous plant to Sri Lanka that contains high medicinal value, worth Rs. 300,000 out of Sri Lanka, was apprehended by Customs officers...

title: Russia pledges to expedite fuel supplies for Sri Lanka, long-term trade deal discussed
byline: A meeting was held between the Deputy Foreign Minister of Russia, Andrey Rudenko, who is currently on an official visit to Sri Lanka, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism, Vijitha Herath, at the Foreign Ministry in Colombo.

title: Two arrested for hoarding over 2,000L of diesel in Thambalagamuwa
byline: Two individuals have been arrested for hoarding a stock of fuel without a valid license in the Mollipothana area of Thambalagamuwa.

title: Babies evacuated from Gaza two years ago returned to their overjoyed parents
byline: They’ve never known their parents, and they’ve never known Gaza, born prematurely two years ago and evacuated to Egypt as Israeli forces drew dangerously close to their neonatal care unit.

title: Circular issued to manage govt expenditure amid energy crisis
byline: The Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development has issued a circular aimed at managing state expenditure within existing fiscal limits and approved government spending ceilings.

title: Ex-soldier arrested after two including woman murdered in Galle, another critical
byline: A man and a woman were killed, while another woman sustained serious injuries and was admitted to Karapitiya Hospital following an alleged attack in Thelikada, Galle.

title: Doctors to strike in hospitals island-wide from tomorrow - GMOA
byline: Government doctors in all hospitals across the island will engage in a strike action from 8:00 a.m. tomorrow (April 4), the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) announced.

title: “Walk for Peace” that captivated millions in US to begin in Sri Lanka with state patronage
byline: A discussion on providing state patronage for the “Walk for Peace Programme in Sri Lanka” was held at the Presidential Secretariat, with the participation of a group of Venerable monks who undertook a 110-day peace walk across 10 states from Texas to Washington in the United States.

title: Pakistan raises fuel prices by 43%
byline: Pakistan’s government has raised petrol prices by 43% and high speed diesel by 55% overnight, saying it was due to increasing oil prices caused by the war in Iran.

title: No issue in releasing water for cultivation in upcoming ‘Yala’ season: Irrigation Dept.
byline: The Department of Irrigation says that there will be no issue in releasing water for paddy fields during the upcoming ‘Yala’ season this year.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for tomorrow
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Eastern, North-Western, Northern and North-Central provinces and in the Monaragala District.

title: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing elected president by pro-military parliament
byline: Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing was elected president on Friday after breezing through a parliamentary vote, formalising his grip on political power in the war-torn nation five years after he ousted an elected government in a coup.

title: New Peaky Blinders TV series to star Jamie Bell
byline: Actor Jamie Bell is set to star in the new TV series of Peaky Blinders, which will be set in the 1950s.

title: Catholic churches in Dubai cancel masses, citing government directives
byline: Catholic churches in Dubai say they have cancelled masses ahead of the Easter weekend on the instructions of the government.

title: Journalist Bhakti Dharmapriya Mendis passes away
byline: Veteran journalist Bhakti Dharmapriya Mendis, who had been receiving treatment at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of the National Hospital in Colombo after sustaining serious injuries in a road accident, has passed away.

title: Over 500 arrested in island-wide anti-drug operations
byline: A total of 512 individuals have been arrested during a series of search operations carried out islandwide under crime and drug prevention raids.

title: Iran confirms the death of IRGC Navy intelligence chief
byline: Iran’s IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) has confirmed the death of Behnam Rezaei, head of the IRGC Navy Intelligence Directorate, in a statement today.

title: 147 foreign nationals remanded over online financial scams
byline: A total of 147 foreign nationals who were arrested in connection with an online financial fraud have been remanded until April 09, 2026.

title: US fighter jet shot down over Iran, search underway for crew, US official says
byline: A U.S. fighter jet was shot down over Iran and a search and rescue operation ⁠was underway for any survivors, a U.S. official told Reuters on Friday.

title: World food price rise set to continue if Iran war lasts, FAO says
byline: World food prices climbed in March to their highest level since September last year and could rise further if the Middle East conflict that pushed up energy prices continues, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization said on Friday.

title: Expert committee appointed to restructure and upgrade National Colleges of Education
byline: A committee of experts has been appointed to enhance the standards and undertake the restructuring of National Colleges of Education.

title: Icons of Sri Lanka among top finalists in UK-based 21st Century’s Global Merit Index
byline: In an era marked by unprecedented technological advance, seismic social change, and deepening global interdependence, South Asia’s most transformative minds and hearts are now part of a ground-breaking and momentous global reckoning of influence.

title: Water cut duration reduced to 18 hours - NWSDB
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has decided to reduce the duration of the scheduled water supply interruptions to 18 hours, taking into consideration the requests made by consumers.

title: DV Chanaka claims Energy Minister trying to suppress substandard coal import report
byline: SLPP Parliamentarian D.V. Chanaka has alleged that the Energy Minister is making strenuous efforts to prevent the publication of the report related to substandard coal imports.

title: Four inmates escape from Kandakadu rehabilitation centre
byline: A total of four inmates have reportedly escaped from the Kandakadu Treatment and Rehabilitation Centre in Polonnaruwa.

title: Netanyahu claims 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity destroyed
byline: Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday (April 3, 2026) that Israeli strikes have destroyed about 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity, significantly hindering its ability to manufacture weapons.

title: NASA releases first Earth photos from Artemis II Orion
byline: The Artemis II crew on Friday shared an image of Earth from the spaceship embarking on first lunar voyage in more than half a century.

title: Iranian parliament speaker mocks US over downed jet
byline: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has mocked the US on his X account after reports that an American fighter jet was shot down over Iran.

title: Over 500 families affected by water shortage in Rukmalgama Housing Scheme
byline: More than 500 families living in the Rukmalgama Housing Scheme are reportedly facing severe difficulties due to a lack of water for several days amid prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: One crew member from downed US fighter jet rescued - US officials
byline: One crew member from the downed F-15 fighter jet has been rescued, two US officials have told CBS News.
